messages:
olivia: Quick follow-up on the manifest decoupling RFC — TL;DR: propose moving quant profiles out of model artifacts into a separate versioned manifest service so runtime only pulls a manifest ID. Thoughts on migration and compatibility?

raj: I like the separation. main concerns: telemetry continuity and calibration drift when manifests change. need a way to tie historical tokens -> manifest_id for post-hoc analysis.

mike: Ops perspective: we need a clear rollback path if a new manifest causes quality regressions. Can we keep runtime support for an explicit fallback list in the request envelope? e.g. manifest_id + fallback_manifest_ids[] so runtime can gracefully degrade without operator intervention.

dana: Perf test note: switching manifests can change memory layout (quant offsets, scale factors) and affect KV cache hit patterns. We should run a small A/B for cold/warm KV states. Also consider a stale-detection metric when observed quality deviates beyond threshold.

olivia: Agreed on rollback/fallback. Proposal: manifest: { id, version, model_compat: [arch+shape tags], validation_hash, quality_anchor } runtime config: accept manifest_id or manifest_bundle (for pinned) and optional fallbacks. For telemetry, stamp every request with manifest_id, model_hash, and calibration_seed so we can slice.

raj: For calibration_seed — do we mean a deterministic calibration fingerprint derived from the manifest + model? That would help group tokens. Also add manifest_epoch timestamp for temporal queries.

mike: Operational checklist: 1) manifest service deployed read-only to runtime 2) runtime fetch logic: cached + TTL + ETag 3) fallback ordering for low-latency failover 4) canary rollout plan and quick disable API.

dana: Can we add a lightweight local validation before switching to new manifest? something like: sample 10 shadow inferences with new manifest keys and compute a tiny quality delta score using eval hooks; if delta > threshold > abort. Cheap and fast to avoid large regressions.

olivia: Exactly — add a preflight endpoint: /manifest/:id/preflight which the runtime or canary infra can call with a small prompt set. returns {delta_histogram, stat: pass/fail}. Preflight results stored in manifest metadata.

raj: Another interface question: per-customer overrides. Some customers need strict numeric parity. We should allow an "enforce_profile": "strict|suggested|opt-in" flag. strict => runtime must refuse any manifest that isn't exact match with customer's pinned manifest. suggested => runtime may fall back.

mike: That aligns with Dedicated/Private requirements. Also record chargeback: if fallback to higher-precision happens, attribute cost delta to customer. We need billing signals.

dana: Telemetry hooks: add per-request fields: manifest_id, manifest_version, preflight_result_id, fallback_reason. And an aggregator that flags sudden shifts in distribution (token perplexity, entropy, repeated stop tokens).

olivia: Implementation plan (short): Phase 1: manifest service + schema v1, runtime accepts manifest_id and caches. Phase 2: preflight endpoint + telemetry stamping. Phase 3: fallback/fallback-order + canary rollout and per-tenant policy flags. Phase 4: Ops tooling for rollback + billing signals.

raj: One more: migration path for existing models with embedded profiles. We can publish a migration tool that extracts embedded profiles into manifests and emits a mapping table model_hash -> manifest_id. Runtime will read mapping table until customers re-pin.

mike: For rollout, let's require a 24h shadow window where new manifests are shadowed on 1-5% of traffic and we run the preflight checks continuously. If no regressions, promote.

dana: Add a linting step on manifest CI: enforce quant metadata (scale ranges, zero-point heuristics), disallow silent truncation modes unless explicitly allowed.

olivia: Nice. I'll draft a short follow-up doc with schema examples and the ops playbook. If folks can ping any missing edgecases now.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: manifest-service/staging deployed to r-quant-manifests-2 at 2024-03-12T18:12:04Z :rocket: 

raj: One nit: make sure we version the validation hash algorithm in the manifest (so old hashes can still be interpreted).

mike: +1. Also add a simple CLI to force-apply manifest with dry-run mode for Private customers.

dana: I'll prepare the small eval prompt set and a perf microbench for warm/cold cache comparisons.

olivia: Great, I'll share the draft in the RFC follow-up doc and tag you all. Thanks!
